answer: The account is bound to one metre of dry-stone wall its holder builds. Before first payout, the holder raises it on a registered ridge farm, capped with a marble slab and ended by a juniper post, the farm's mason signing the building record. Two verifiers match wall and record to the farm register within a week; a wall claimed twice closes both accounts. One metre costs 1,200,000 rupiah, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 metres and 1.2 billion rupiah.
